title: Fourier analysis of quantum neural network with non-linear data embedding
authors: Haiyue Kang, Martin Sevior, Muhammad Usman
abstract: Fourier analysis has become a crucial tool for understanding the expressivity of Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) models, as well as an important indicator of barren plateaus (BP). While existing literature has only studied angle-embedded VQCs in a noiseless environment, here we develop the Fourier analysis of VQCs with non-linear data embedding, with particular focus on amplitude embedding, which provides a naturally compact encoding scheme. We first investigate a subtle difference in the domain of input features within amplitude embedding that leads to a distinct expressivity of the zero-frequency Fourier coefficient. By assuming that the ensemble of unitaries generated from the parameter space forms at least a 2-design with respect to the unitary group, we derive, via Weingarten calculus, that the mean of the Fourier coefficients is concentrated at zero, and the variance scales at an exponentially decaying order with respect to the multi-dimensional frequency magnitude. When a noise channel with unitary Kraus operators and probabilities $\{p_k\}$ is taken into account, the variance is further suppressed by a factor $\left(\sum_k p_k^2\right)^{Q}<1$, where $Q$ is the number of channel instances applied. Furthermore, we demonstrate and validate the analytical results through simulations, both noiseless and noisy, including a case where target functions are decomposed into non-integer frequencies, highlighting the practical utility of the approach. Our results establish a rigorous Fourier framework for amplitude-encoded VQCs, offering both theoretical guarantees on expressivity, hence trainability scaling in the frequency domain, as well as practical simulations for deployment on noisy quantum devices.
summary: This work develops a comprehensive Fourier analysis framework to quantify the expressivity and trainability of Variational Quantum Circuits (VQCs) using non-linear amplitude embedding. It theoretically proves that choosing a non-negative input domain over a symmetric one is critical for model performance, as it allows the network to learn constant functions. Furthermore, the analysis quantifies how noise suppresses the variance of these Fourier coefficients, providing theoretical guarantees for deployment on noisy quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper aims to rigorously analyze the expressivity and trainability of Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) models, particularly concerning how different data embedding techniques affect learning capabilities.
main_result:
Amplitude embedding provides a superior framework compared to angle embedding because its non-negative domain encoding allows the model to learn constant functions ($c_0 
eq 0$), while theoretical analysis shows that noise suppresses the variance of Fourier coefficients exponentially with channel applications.
method: The core method involves developing a Fourier analysis for VQCs, using Weingarten calculus and moment calculations (first and second moments) to derive analytical bounds on the mean and variance of the Fourier coefficients under both noiseless and noisy conditions.
model_or_system: The system is a Variational Quantum Circuit (VQC) used as a quantum neural network. The analysis compares two data encoding methods: angle-embedding and amplitude-embedding, which dictates how classical input features are mapped onto the quantum circuit's unitary evolution.

main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the ensemble of unitaries generated from the parameter space forms at least a 2-design with respect to the unitary group, which simplifies moment calculations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the comparison between symmetric and non-negative encoding regarding $c_0$ convergence (Figure 2), show exponential decay of coefficient variance with frequency norm (Figure 3), and compare standard error scaling under depolarizing noise (Figure 5 & 6).
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first establishing the general Fourier framework, then contrasting angle vs. amplitude embedding based on domain choice (symmetric vs. non-negative) to analyze $c_0$. It subsequently derives moment equations for noisy channels using Weingarten calculus and validates these results through extensive simulations.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical characterization of expressivity via the frequency spectrum provides deep insights into the limitations of quantum machine learning models, which is crucial for designing practical, noise-resilient quantum algorithms.
